issue_context.title: to_numpy returns the same list for all rows
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
import numpy as np
import polars as pl

df = pl.DataFrame({"a": [[4, 5, 6], [7, 8, 9, 10]]})
assert (df[1].to_numpy()[0][0] == np.array([4, 5, 6, 7])).all()
```


### Log output

_No response_

### Issue description

When storing lists in the dataframe, indexing via square brackets combined with to_numpy returns an element of correct length, but with the first values of all lists concatenated

### Expected behavior

The given example should return [7, 8, 9. 10] instead of weirdly concatenating [4, 5, 6] to [7, 8, 9, 10] and taking the length of the element.

### Installed versions

<details>

```
--------Version info---------
Polars:              1.8.2
Index type:          UInt32
Platform:            Linux-5.15.0-94-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.35
Python:              3.10.12 (main, Jul 29 2024, 16:56:48) [GCC 11.4.0]

----Optional dependencies----
```

comments:
Can reproduce.

It only seems to be happening for `Series -> Numpy`

```python
list(df[1].item())
# [7, 8, 9, 10]

df[1].to_numpy()
# array([array([4, 5, 6, 7])], dtype=object)
```

Frame-level `.to_numpy()` does not seem affected.

```python
df.to_numpy()[1]
# array([array([ 7,  8,  9, 10])], dtype=object)
```

review_comments: This is wrong for 2 reasons. The slicing was incorrect, but it also doesn't include null values and can show masked out values.
